title: correction_cycles is the only new detail key decoded without null tolerance — a null value fails the whole payload decode
evidence:
+  use correction_cycles <- decode.optional_field(
+    "correction_cycles",
+    0,
+    decode.int,
+  )

vs every sibling key:
+  use contact_phone <- decode.optional_field(
+    "contact_phone",
+    None,
+    decode.optional(decode.string),
+  )

and the spec contract: "`correction_cycles` (Option/Int, back-compat `optional_field` decoders). Encoder nullable."
detail: Sibling keys wrap the inner decoder in decode.optional (null → None); correction_cycles uses bare decode.int, so a null value fails the whole detail decode and thus the entire payload. No test covers null, and the spec says 'Encoder nullable'.
recommended_fix: Decode with decode.optional(decode.int) mapped to 0 (or COALESCE server-side) and add a null-tolerance test matching the sibling keys.

title: Spec item 6's additive shared-keys enumeration omits corrected_name, contradicting the migration and code in the same diff
evidence:
6. **`shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam`** — additive detail keys: `taken_over_at`, `contact_name`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`, `corrected_email`, `corrected_phone`, `correction_cycles` (Option/Int, back-compat `optional_field` decoders). Encoder nullable.

but the migration adds it:
+ALTER TABLE reference_call
+  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS corrected_name TEXT;

and the code encodes it:
+    #("corrected_name", json.nullable(detail.corrected_name, json.string)),
detail: Item 6 lists the shared payload keys without corrected_name, while the migration, type, encoder, decoder and tests in this diff all add it (AC3 lists it too). Implementation follows AC3; the enumeration is stale.
recommended_fix: Add corrected_name to the item 6 additive-key list.

title: Correct guard writes correction_cycles = correction_cycles + 1 — if the column is nullable, a NULL stays NULL and the >= 1 exhaustion guard never trips
evidence:
guarded `awaiting_correction → queued` with `corrected_name/email/phone = $n`
     (empty string = NULL), `correction_cycles = correction_cycles + 1`, `next_attempt_at = now()`,
     `terminal_reason = NULL`

...and the exhaustion check:
when the guarded failure transition finds `correction_cycles >= 1`, the row does NOT go to
     `awaiting_correction` again — it terminalizes `→ unreachable`
detail: SQL NULL + 1 = NULL. The reads COALESCE correction_cycles (item 4), so the column may be nullable; a NULL count never satisfies >= 1, a second failure loops back to awaiting_correction, and 'Max 1 cycle' silently breaks.
recommended_fix: Write COALESCE(correction_cycles, 0) + 1 in the correction UPDATE, or pin NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and state nullability in the spec.
